name: Gauḍa Abhinanda
dates_notes: The Laghu-Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha is commonly associated with a Kashmiri Gauḍa Abhinanda. Modern scholarship places the compilation probably in the tenth century but allows a substantially later terminus; proposed identifications with the Rāmacarita poet, Jayanta Bhaṭṭa's son, or an otherwise unknown Abhinanda remain unresolved.
core_thesis: Source-identity record for the Gauḍa Abhinanda associated with the Laghu-Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha. He is not identified here with the South-Indian Krama author represented by the separate `abhinanda` record. The historical identity and date remain contested; this hidden draft exists so citations to the Laghu do not conflate two different Abhinandas.

engaged_works.title: Laghu-Yoga-Vasistha
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Traditionally and conventionally associated with Gauḍa Abhinanda, but the historical identity of that Abhinanda is unresolved.

ascription_evidence.description: The Paṇaśīkara edition identifies an Abhinanda in the work's transmission; modern scholarship describes Gauḍa Abhinanda as the compiler while explicitly retaining uncertainty over which historical Abhinanda he was.

engaged_works.summary: A roughly five-to-six-thousand-verse reworking and abridgment of the Kashmiri Mokṣopāya. The present reader covers the complete concise Dāmādyupākhyāna at Sthitiprakaraṇa 2.31–86.

reception_notes: Hidden source-identity record; not admitted as a separate public timeline figure pending a dedicated authorship and chronology review.
